info.title: MSC 2 v1 API contract
info.description: The versioned HTTP contract MSC 2's skeletal agent (Phase 2) and every later phase implement against. Assembled per docs/msc2/rolling-plan.md P2.8 from the P0.23/P0.30/P0.32 MSC 1 baseline (docs/msc2/api-baseline/openapi.json) plus this phase's own designs: the /v1/ namespace and ErrorDTO envelope (P2.4, versioning-and-errors.md), the operation routes and OperationDTO (P2.5, operation-model.md), the capabilities route (P2.6, capability-model.md), helpId placement (P2.2, helpid-contract.md), and the permission-category annotation on every route (P2.1, permission-vocabulary.csv). Phase 10 extends the shared routes additively for Bedrock runtime state, without adding a parallel /v1/bedrock route family. The console and operation-progress WebSocket channels (P2.7) are documented separately in docs/msc2/api-contract/websocket-v1.json, matching the baseline's own precedent (P0.24) of keeping WS channels out of the OpenAPI paths object. Everything sourced from P2.4/P2.5/P2.6/P2.2's own documents carries their Proposed/Confirmed status forward -- this file does not itself promote anything to Approved.

post.summary: Create a new server

200.description: Server creation started (bedrock: capability_unavailable is returned as 409 instead, see x-notes)

400.description: missing_body / invalid_json / name_required / invalid_server_type / invalid_java_flavor / unsupported_server_type

409.description: create_failed / capability_unavailable (Bedrock create, refused rather than half-provisioned; Phase 10)

post.x-notes: P7.9 correction to this note's own P2.8-era wording: 'runs async via createServerProvider' described MSC 1's Swift-Task mechanism, not wire behavior -- MSC 1's own handleCreateServer holds the HTTP response open until createServerProvider fully returns (RemoteAPIServer+ComponentRoutes.swift:87-112), which blocks the connection for the real minutes a Forge/NeoForge install-step create can take (corpus/providers' captured installer runs, P7.3). Phase 7 corrects this under D-006's 'correction' clause: after name/type/flavor validation and (for Bedrock) the capability_unavailable refusal, the 200 response returns immediately with serverId/serverName (known synchronously -- folder derivation is a pure function of the trimmed name, families/phase7-scope.md SS 'Cross-family creation mechanics' step 2) and a populated operationId; warnings and final success/failure land on the operation's own terminal result (operation-model.md SS2), not on this response. A client that only reads success/message/serverId/serverName keeps working; one that wants progress or cancellation follows operationId. type: "server-create". A failed or cancelled operation leaves the server directory rolled back completely (this phase's working exit criteria), matching the create_failed 409 MSC 1 already returns for the synchronous validation failures that still happen before the operation is admitted. P8.9: stagedModpackUploadId is additive and optional -- when present, this same durable create operation also pins the loader/Minecraft version from the pack and applies its mod list (P8.21), and does not publish the server registry entry until pack application succeeds too, extending the existing create-rollback discipline to a failure class MSC 1's own creation flow could never roll back from (phase8-scope.md, "Modpack create/import boundary"). type stays "server-create".

post.summary: Update a system component (paper/geyser/floodgate) or a Modrinth-tracked add-on
post.x-notes: Seven request shapes now share one endpoint (RemoteAPIServer+ComponentRoutes.swift's own handleUpdateComponent precedent, extended per P8.9): updateAll=true updates every add-on with an available update (async, 202); jarStem alone updates one specific add-on (async, 202); jarStem+enabled toggles it (sync, 200, togglePlugin/toggleMod); jarStem+linkProjectId manually links it to a Modrinth project (sync, 200, manuallyLinkAddon); jarStem+sourceUrl sets/replaces its plugin source (sync, 200, setPluginSource); jarStem+removeSource removes one (sync, 200, removePluginSource); the legacy component=paper|geyser|floodgate path updates a system component (sync, 200, ComponentUpdateResultDTO). All six add-on shapes are refused (409 conflict, code pack_managed) against a pack-managed server; the explicit escape hatch is POST /v1/modpacks/import {action: "replace"}, not any shape of this route.

200.description: Synchronous shapes only (toggle/link/source-set/source-remove): updateAll/jarStem-update shapes instead return 202 (see below) once request shape and the pack-managed guard pass.

202.description: updateAll/jarStem-update shapes only: update admitted and started. result/count land on the operation's terminal AddonUpdateResultDTO.

409.description: not_supported (jarStem path) / pack_managed (ErrorDTO.details carries packName/packVersion; applies to every shape below except the legacy component=paper|geyser|floodgate path, which never touches an add-on)

Install an add-on from the Modrinth catalog into the active server

202.description: Install admitted and started (including a local-JAR install via stagedUploadId). success/message/count/installedDependencies land on the operation's terminal result; a client that ignores operationId and only reads the body still gets a truthful in-flight message, not a final result.

post.x-notes: Corrected per P8.9 (D-006 point 3, same class of correction P7.9 applied to servers/create and components/version): a catalog install can cost real Modrinth network time, and P8.15's dependency-aware batch install can cost several. The 202 response returns once request shape, staged-upload redemption (if stagedUploadId was used), and the pack-managed guard all pass; operation type: "addon-install".

post.summary: Change the active server's JAR version/build
post.x-notes: MSC 1's own changeVersionProvider comment calls this 'authoritative-async (awaits the real result)' -- in wire terms that means the baseline HTTP handler blocks the connection until the download, or for NeoForge/Forge the full supervised installer subprocess (real minutes, P7.3's captured installer runs), finishes (AppViewModel+APIWiringAddons.swift:358-573). Phase 7 applies the same correction as /v1/servers/create: the 200 response returns as soon as the existing isDownloadingJar-equivalent admission check passes, carrying a populated operationId; success/failure/requiresRestart land on the operation's terminal result. type: "version-change". The existing download_in_progress 429 is preserved unchanged (D-006: preserve rate-limiting intent) as the same-server concurrent-request guard it always was -- a second request while one operation is already running for this server still gets 429, it just now names an operation instead of a raw in-flight download.

post.summary: Inspect a staged modpack archive (.mrpack or CurseForge) without mutating any server
post.x-notes: Redeems nothing -- the one deliberate exception to 'a staging slot can only be redeemed by the route it was created for once' (worlds.rs's own doc comment): inspect peeks at a modpack-archive-purpose staged upload without marking it consumed, so the same upload can be inspected and then imported (POST /v1/modpacks/import) or carried into server creation (ServerCreateRequestDTO.stagedModpackUploadId) without a second upload round-trip. The upload still expires on its ordinary expiresAt -- inspecting it does not extend its lifetime.

404.description: staged upload not found, expired, or not purpose modpack-archive

post.summary: Import a staged modpack archive into the active server, or explicitly replace an already pack-managed server's pack
post.x-notes: Redeems the staged upload (purpose modpack-archive) for real -- unlike inspect, above. Returns 202 as soon as the upload is verified, the archive is re-validated, and (for action=replace) the pack-managed check passes; downloading, overrides-merge, and classification continue in a background worker, type: "modpack-import". Author-blocked CurseForge files pause this operation at a checkpoint (state stays running, ModpackImportResultDTO.pendingManualFiles/statusLine name what's pending) until every one is resolved via POST /v1/modpacks/{operationId}/manual-file (D-027) -- there is no separate paused state in operation-model.md's closed state machine, so this is running with a checkpoint, not a new state.

404.description: staged upload not found, expired, or not purpose modpack-archive

409.description: no_active_server / pack_managed (action=import against an already pack-managed server, or action=replace against one that isn't -- ErrorDTO.details carries packName/packVersion)

post.summary: Complete one pending author-blocked CurseForge file for a running modpack-import operation (D-027)
post.x-notes: The one manual-file completion route this phase's D-027 answer (option 1, msc2-decisions.md) commits to: the client downloads the blocked file itself from CurseForge's own web page, stages it (POST /v1/staged-uploads {purpose: curseforge-manual-file, operationId, fileId}), then calls this route to bind and verify it against the pending operation's own expected file identity/size before the background worker resumes. Synchronous -- binding and verifying one already-uploaded file is a local check, not a download; the modpack-import operation itself keeps running in the background once every pending file is resolved.

404.description: unknown operationId, operation not a pending modpack-import, unknown fileId, or staged upload not found/expired/wrong purpose

409.description: wrong file for this fileId (hash/size/name mismatch against CurseForge's own recorded metadata -- ErrorDTO.details carries expectedFileId/expectedFileName/expectedByteSize)

post.summary: Install a Java runtime the agent manages itself

429.description: download_in_progress (an install for this major is already running)

post.x-notes: New route, P7.1's dated addendum to D-006 (Cameron's answer to 'Questions before P7.1': MSC 2 installs Java itself). No MSC 1 equivalent -- JavaInstaller.swift's installerURL/downloadInstaller fetch a macOS-only Temurin .pkg for a human to double-click (families/phase7-scope.md, 'Java runtime install'), which this route does not port. Request names only `major` (one of the four JavaInstaller.minecraftInstallOptions values, P7.7); OS/architecture are never client-supplied -- the agent always installs a runtime for its own host (D-009: MSC 2 owns its own runtime state). Always async: like POST /v1/worlds/convert, there is no synchronous variant, so operationId is required on the result rather than optional. type: "java-download" (the type name operation-model.md SS2 already anticipated). Unpacks under MSC's own runtimes directory, never a system Java location; an interrupted install leaves nothing behind (families/phase7-scope.md's rollback-discipline note). A second install request for a major already installing gets the same download_in_progress 429 vocabulary /v1/components/version uses, not a new code.

post.summary: Start a Chunker world-format conversion
post.x-notes: Always operation-backed (operation-model.md SS2's type: world-conversion, named there as an anticipated future type). Guard order, temp cleanup, and the two flagged D-006 gaps (replaceSlotWithConvertedZip's non-atomic archive replacement; the pre-conversion backup's warn-only failure) are characterized in fixtures/world-conversion, not re-litigated here. Corrected post-review: targetFormat is validated against the installed Chunker jar's own supported-format list (400 invalid_body, code unsupported_target_format, if not); exactly one of targetName/targetSlotId is required (400 invalid_body otherwise); targetServerId names a server that may differ from the one sourceSlotId resolves against.

409.description: sole_verified_backup -- Phase 6's retention-floor correction: MSC 1's count-based pruning has no floor against deleting the last remaining verified backup (fixtures/backups), this route does.

post.summary: Begin a bounded staged upload
post.x-notes: SS4: staged upload/download replaces an arbitrary remote path with a short-lived, purpose-bound, size-bound token. Approved-root enforcement and request-size limits are P6.21 wiring, not designed further here. P8.9 correction: x-permission-category was worlds (Phase 6, the only domain that existed yet); moved to none. Staging bytes alone commits nothing -- each purpose's redemption route already enforces its own correct category (worlds for world-import/active-world-replace, addons for modpack-archive/addon-local-file/curseforge-manual-file) -- so a single fixed category on the shared begin/upload routes was already wrong the moment a second domain needed the same primitive; an addons-only token could stage nothing at all under the old category. Redemption-side enforcement is unchanged.

Staging bytes alone commits nothing -- each purpose's redemption route already enforces its own correct category (worlds for world-import/active-world-replace, addons for modpack-archive/addon-local-file/curseforge-manual-file) -- so a single fixed category on the shared begin/upload routes was already wrong the moment a second domain needed the same primitive; an addons-only token could stage nothing at all under the old category. Redemption-side enforcement is unchanged.

bedrockVersion.description: Requested BDS release for serverType=bedrock. The agent resolves and verifies the platform-appropriate distribution entry.

stagedModpackUploadId.description: A staged upload (purpose modpack-archive) already inspected via POST /v1/modpacks/inspect. When present, provisioning pins the loader/Minecraft version from the pack and applies its mod list as part of this same create operation (P8.21) -- MSC 1 has no separate create-from-pack primitive; this mirrors createNewServer + applyStagedAddOn composed into one durable operation instead of two.

operationId.description: Phase 4 lifecycle operation id for progress polling or /v1/operations/{id}/stream; optional so older clients can ignore it.

runtime.description: Optional Bedrock runtime state. Older clients may ignore this additive field.

sourcePath.description: Required for scan/importExisting/importTransfer; omitted for rescan, which scans the configured servers root.

runtime.description: Optional Bedrock runtime state for the imported record.

operationId.description: Operation id for progress polling (GET /v1/operations/{id}) or /v1/operations/{id}/stream and cancellation; optional so older clients can ignore it, matching SimpleResult's P4 precedent.

enabled.description: With jarStem and no updateAll/component: enable/disable that add-on (togglePlugin/toggleMod).

linkProjectId.description: With jarStem: manually link this add-on to a Modrinth project id (manuallyLinkAddon). Sets AddonLinkProvenance.nameGuess.

sourceUrl.description: With jarStem: set/replace this add-on's plugin source (GitHub/Hangar/direct URL, classified the same way PluginSourceDetector.detect does). setPluginSource.

removeSource.description: With jarStem: remove a previously-set plugin source (removePluginSource).

operationId.description: Present only for the update-triggering shapes (updateAll, jarStem update) -- these download real bytes and run async. Absent for toggle/link/source-set/source-remove, which stay synchronous (a config or filesystem-rename change, no network fetch).

stagedUploadId.description: Install from a staged local JAR (purpose addon-local-file) instead of the catalog. Exactly one of {projectId+slug+title} or stagedUploadId must be given -- not both, not neither.

operationId.description: Operation id for progress polling (GET /v1/operations/{id}) or /v1/operations/{id}/stream and cancellation; optional so older clients can ignore it.

installedDependencies.description: jarStems of required dependencies installed alongside the requested add-on (P8.15's bounded dependency installer). Empty when the add-on had none.

operationId.description: Phase 7 addition (P7.9): operation id for progress polling or /v1/operations/{id}/stream and cancellation; optional so older clients can ignore it, same pattern as ServerCreateResultDTO.operationId.

runtime.description: Optional Bedrock runtime state after a version request.
Optional runtime state while backup settings are read.
Optional runtime state after backup settings are applied.

operationId.description: Operation id for progress polling (GET /v1/operations/{id}) or /v1/operations/{id}/stream and cancellation; optional so older clients can ignore it, matching SimpleResult's P4 precedent.

runtime.description: Optional runtime state for the backup operation.

operationId.description: Operation id for progress polling (GET /v1/operations/{id}) or /v1/operations/{id}/stream and cancellation; optional so older clients can ignore it, matching SimpleResult's P4 precedent.

runtime.description: Optional runtime state for the restore operation.

helpId.description: Keyed off kind, e.g. diagnostics.crash.forge-dep (helpid-contract.md SS4).

operationId.description: Present only when action is update/install (P8.23 -- these route through the same verified add-on mutation paths as ordinary install/update, so they cost the same real download time). Absent for disable/delete, which stay the existing synchronous rename/removal.
Present when helper work continues; poll GET /v1/operations/{id} or stream its progress.
Present when the staged download continues after this response.
Present when helper lifecycle work continues after this response.

runtime.description: Optional runtime state for a Bedrock command result.

operationId.description: Phase 4 lifecycle operation id for progress polling or /v1/operations/{id}/stream; optional so older clients can ignore it.

runtime.description: Optional Bedrock runtime state associated with the lifecycle request.
Optional Bedrock runtime state; file reads may remain available while the runtime is unavailable.
Optional Bedrock runtime state for the player data source.
Optional current Bedrock runtime state for an imported or created server.
Optional runtime state for the active Bedrock server.
Optional runtime state for this performance source.

note.description: Set for a component this build honestly cannot check yet (e.g. Geyser/Floodgate update checks stay Phase 9) instead of a fabricated isUpToDate/updatable value.

stagedDownloadId.description: Set only for exportKind=zip. Redeem via GET /v1/staged-downloads/{id} (P6.8's staged-download primitive), the same mechanism POST /v1/worlds/export already uses -- not inline base64, which would roughly double a large modded pack's response size.

note.description: Set when a provider was unreachable during this resolve pass (provider_unavailable) -- addons still reflect last-known persisted state, not a fabricated fresh result.

major.description: One of JavaInstaller.minecraftInstallOptions' four majors (8/17/21/25, P7.7). OS/architecture are never client-supplied -- the agent always installs for its own host (D-009).

operationId.description: Always populated -- this route has no synchronous variant, same as WorldConvertResultDTO.operationId.

runtime.description: Optional runtime state for the active server's backup source.

helpId.description: Replaces the baseline's free-text help field (helpid-contract.md SS4) -- resolves via GET /v1/help/{helpId}.

runtime.description: Optional runtime state; settings can be readable before a runtime is runnable.
Optional Bedrock runtime state after settings are applied.

BedrockRuntimeStateDTO.description: Phase 10 runtime disclosure shared by existing v1 DTOs. It describes the current Bedrock backend state, not the separate published compatibility matrix.

helpId.description: Optional educational topic for the runtime reason.

ErrorDTO.description: One error envelope for every non-2xx response across every /v1/ route (P2.4 SS5-6, a D-006-point-3 correction unifying the baseline's split Error/typed-DTO failure pattern).

code.description: Stable machine-readable snake_case identifier, e.g. not_found, conflict, invalid_body.

details.description: Optional free-form structured context. Bedrock capability_unavailable responses use the listed fields when present.

OperationDTO.description: P2.5 SS2 -- the wire shape for a long-running operation.

type.description: Kind of work, e.g. demo-install. Not a closed enum -- new values are additive (P2.5 SS2).

target.description: The thing the operation acts on, typically a server name/ID. Null if the operation type has no natural target.

progress.description: Null while queued, or for a type with no natural countable unit.

cancelable.description: Optional additive disclosure. False once a stop operation has entered graceful termination or another operation-specific non-cancelable boundary.

result.description: Present only when state == succeeded. Shape defined per type.

type.description: Required. Unrecognized values are a 400 invalid_body.

permissions.description: The calling token's granted categories, per D-019's nine-bucket vocabulary (Proposed).

runtime.description: Authoritative current runtime state; supported/backend remain for older clients.

serverTypes.description: Java flags and Bedrock runtime state are host capabilities. Bedrock uses the separate D-022 compatibility matrix for published evidence.

helpers.description: Placeholder this phase (P2.6 SS3) -- real presence detection is Phase 3 substrate work.

body.description: Raw Markdown. Clients render; they do not author (D-026 point 1).

PerformanceMetricNumberDTO.description: P2.8's resolution of helpid-contract.md SS4's open item: PerformanceSnapshotDTO's bare scalars wrap into {value, helpId} (option b) rather than a separate static client-side name->helpId map (option a) -- consistent with every other helpId-bearing DTO in this contract attaching the pointer directly on the field's own object, at the cost of a DTO-shape change from the baseline. Proposed, pending Cameron's confirmation.

WorldRenameActiveWorldRequestDTO.description: Direct rename of the active/live world's on-disk folders (AppViewModel+WorldManagement.swift's renameWorld) -- distinct from WorldRenameRequestDTO, which renames a slot's metadata only and touches no files.

stagedUploadId.description: Redeems a staged upload begun with purpose "active-world-replace" as the replacement world's source ZIP. Omit to replace with a fresh (empty) world instead -- never an arbitrary server-local path.

WorldReplaceActiveRequestDTO.description: AppViewModel+WorldManagement.swift's replaceWorld -- direct live-world replacement. Separately named from WorldReplaceRequestDTO (WorldSlotManager.copySlotIntoExisting, a saved-slot-to-saved-slot copy that never touches the live world); see phase6-api.md SS9/SS10.

operationId.description: Operation id for progress polling (GET /v1/operations/{id}) or /v1/operations/{id}/stream and cancellation; optional so older clients can ignore it, matching SimpleResult's P4 precedent.

WorldReplaceActiveResultDTO.description: Always operation-backed: the mandatory pre-replace safety backup and (for an uploaded source) zip staging are real filesystem work, the same class as activate/backups-restore.

WorldConvertRequestDTO.description: Corrected post-review: MSC 1 conversion always names a separate, opposite-edition target server (AppViewModel+WorldConversion.swift's own sourceServer/targetServer parameters) -- sourceSlotId resolves against the active server; targetServerId is a separate, required server id. targetFormat is the exact Chunker format string the client chose from the installed jar's own supported list (MSC 1's wizard defaults its picker to the newest compatible format but always lets the user override it -- never hardcoded server-side). Exactly one of targetName (place into a fresh slot) or targetSlotId (overwrite an existing slot on the target server, by id, not display name) must be present.

WorldConvertResultDTO.description: Always operation-backed (type: world-conversion, operation-model.md SS2) -- Chunker's process lifetime makes this the one Phase 6 world mutation with no synchronous variant.

operationId.description: Required, curseforge-manual-file only: the pending modpack-import operation this upload resumes. The agent looks up the expected file's own reported byte size/name from CurseForge's file metadata already recorded against that operation -- maxBytes on the result is sized to that exact file, not a flat ceiling.

fileId.description: Required, curseforge-manual-file only: which of the operation's pending blocked files this upload is for.

uploadPath.description: PUT /v1/staged-uploads/{id} -- bounded to this token, not an arbitrary remote path.

format.description: Unrecognized archives are a 400, not a 200 with a format value -- there is no third case to represent here.

clientOnlyFileCount.description: Files this pack's own precedence chain (manifest/Modrinth/embedded-jar/known-list, phase8-scope.md) will skip or disable -- reported so a client can show 'N files' vs 'N will actually install' before committing to import.

manualFiles.description: CurseForge files this pack references whose authors block API distribution (D-027). Empty for an mrpack, or a CurseForge pack with no blocked files.

action.description: import: the active server is not yet pack-managed. replace: an explicit whole-pack replacement of an already pack-managed server. Sending import against an already pack-managed server, or replace against one that isn't, is refused as ambiguous (409 conflict) -- the client must know and say which case this is, never guessed server-side.

pendingManualFiles.description: Populated once the operation reaches its blocked-file checkpoint (statusLine names it too); resolve each via POST /v1/modpacks/{operationId}/manual-file. Empty when the pack has no blocked files.
